questions.question: Which of the following structural isomers of $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}$ gives a positive 2,4-DNP test and is the most reactive towards nucleophilic addition reactions?
questions.solution:
Compounds with the molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}$ that give a positive 2,4-DNP test are aldehydes and ketones. The acyclic carbonyl isomers are butanal, 2-methylpropanal, and butan-2-one. Ethoxyethene is an ether and does not give the 2,4-DNP test.

Reactivity towards nucleophilic addition depends on steric hindrance and electronic effects (+I effect). Aldehydes are generally more reactive than ketones due to less steric hindrance and having only one alkyl group donating electron density. Thus, butanal and 2-methylpropanal are more reactive than butan-2-one.

Between butanal and 2-methylpropanal, the latter has a bulky isopropyl group attached directly to the carbonyl carbon, providing more steric hindrance than the straight propyl chain in butanal. Therefore, butanal is the most reactive.

Answer: Butanal

questions.solution:
The final product is 2-phenylbut-2-enoic acid, which has the structure $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{C}(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)-\text{COOH}$.

Working backwards, the double bond is formed by the dehydration of an $\alpha$-hydroxy acid. Adding water across the double bond places the $-\text{OH}$ group at the $\alpha$-carbon, giving 2-hydroxy-2-phenylbutanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}(\text{OH})(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)-\text{COOH}$.

The $-\text{COOH}$ group is formed by the acidic hydrolysis of a nitrile ($-\text{CN}$) group. Replacing $-\text{COOH}$ with $-\text{CN}$ gives the cyanohydrin intermediate, $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}(\text{OH})(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)-\text{CN}$.

This cyanohydrin is formed by the nucleophilic addition of HCN to a carbonyl compound. Removing HCN reveals the original ketone, which is $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CO}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_5$, i.e., 1-phenylpropan-1-one.

Answer: 1-phenylpropan-1-one

Upon separation and acidification of the aqueous layer, sodium propanoate is converted to propanoic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$), which is compound $\text{Y}$.

Answer: Propanoic acid

questions.q:
Identify the correct sequence of reagents to achieve the following transformation:

4-oxohexanal $\rightarrow$ 4-hydroxyhexanoic acid
questions.question:
Identify the correct sequence of reagents to achieve the following transformation:

4-oxohexanal $\rightarrow$ 4-hydroxyhexanoic acid
questions.solution:
To convert 4-oxohexanal to 4-hydroxyhexanoic acid, the aldehyde group must be oxidized to a carboxylic acid and the ketone group must be reduced to a secondary alcohol.

If a reducing agent like $\text{NaBH}_4$ is used first, both the aldehyde and ketone groups will be reduced to alcohols, and Tollens' reagent cannot oxidize alcohols.

Therefore, the aldehyde must be selectively oxidized first. Tollens' reagent ($[\text{Ag}(\text{NH}_3)_2]^+\text{OH}^-$) is a mild oxidizing agent that selectively oxidizes aldehydes to carboxylate salts without affecting ketones.

After oxidation, the intermediate is a keto-carboxylate. Treatment with $\text{NaBH}_4$ selectively reduces the ketone to a secondary alcohol, as $\text{NaBH}_4$ does not reduce carboxylate groups.

Finally, acidic workup ($\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$) protonates the carboxylate to yield the desired 4-hydroxyhexanoic acid.

Answer: (i) $[\text{Ag}(\text{NH}_3)_2]^+\text{OH}^-$ ; (ii) $\text{NaBH}_4\text{, EtOH}$, followed by $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$

(i) Ethylene glycol, dry $HCl$
(ii) Excess $CH_3MgBr$
(iii) $H_3O^+$

The major product formed is:
questions.question:
Ethyl 4-oxopentanoate is subjected to the following sequence of reactions:
(i) Ethylene glycol, dry $HCl$
(ii) Excess $CH_3MgBr$
(iii) $H_3O^+$

The major product formed is:
questions.solution:
The starting material is ethyl 4-oxopentanoate ($CH_3-CO-CH_2-CH_2-COOCH_2CH_3$).

Step (i): Reaction with ethylene glycol and dry $HCl$ selectively protects the ketone group by forming a cyclic acetal (1,3-dioxolane derivative). The ester group remains unreactive under these conditions.

Step (ii): The protected compound is treated with excess $CH_3MgBr$. The Grignard reagent reacts with the ester group. Two equivalents of $CH_3MgBr$ are consumed by the ester to form a tertiary alkoxide ($-C(O^-MgBr^+)(CH_3)_2$).

Step (iii): Acidic workup ($H_3O^+$) serves two purposes. It protonates the alkoxide to yield a tertiary alcohol, and it hydrolyzes the cyclic acetal back to the original ketone.

The final product is $CH_3-CO-CH_2-CH_2-C(OH)(CH_3)_2$, which is named 5-hydroxy-5-methylhexan-2-one.

Answer: 5-Hydroxy-5-methylhexan-2-one

questions.question: Compound X is obtained by the reductive ozonolysis of cyclohexene. When X is heated with dilute aqueous $NaOH$, it undergoes an intramolecular reaction to form a major organic product Y. The total number of $\sigma$ (sigma) bonds in a molecule of Y is ________.
questions.solution:
Reductive ozonolysis of cyclohexene ($O_3$, $Zn/H_2O$) cleaves the double bond to yield hexanedial (X), which is $OHC-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-CHO$.

When hexanedial is heated with dilute aqueous $NaOH$, it undergoes an intramolecular aldol condensation.

The enolate ion formed at the $\alpha$-carbon (C2) attacks the carbonyl carbon (C6) of the other aldehyde group, leading to the formation of a stable five-membered ring.

Subsequent dehydration (loss of $H_2O$) yields cyclopent-1-ene-1-carbaldehyde as the major product (Y).

The molecular formula of cyclopent-1-ene-1-carbaldehyde is $C_6H_8O$.

The structure consists of a five-membered carbon ring with one double bond, and an aldehyde group ($-CHO$) attached to one of the double-bonded ring carbons.

Counting the $\sigma$ (sigma) bonds:
There are $5$ C-C $\sigma$ bonds in the ring and $1$ C-C $\sigma$ bond connecting the ring to the aldehyde group.
There is $1$ C-O $\sigma$ bond in the carbonyl group.
There are $8$ C-H $\sigma$ bonds ($1$ in the aldehyde group, $1$ on the double-bonded ring carbon, and $6$ on the three $CH_2$ groups in the ring).

Total number of $\sigma$ bonds = $6 + 1 + 8 = 15$.

Alternatively, for a molecule with exactly one ring, the total number of $\sigma$ bonds equals the total number of atoms ($6 + 8 + 1 = 15$).

Answer: $15$

2. (2R, 6S) [which is equivalent to (2S, 6R)], which has a plane of symmetry passing through C4, making it an optically inactive meso compound.

Since the addition of HCN to the planar carbonyl groups is non-stereoselective, all these stereoisomers are formed. Thus, the final product mixture contains one meso compound and a pair of enantiomers.

In a crossed Cannizzaro reaction between two different aldehydes lacking \alpha-hydrogens, the initial step is the nucleophilic addition of the hydroxide ion (\text{OH}^-) to the carbonyl carbon.

Therefore, the \text{OH}^- ion attacks p-nitrobenzaldehyde to form a tetrahedral intermediate. This intermediate then acts as a hydride donor, transferring a hydride ion (\text{H}^-) to p-methoxybenzaldehyde.

As a result, the aldehyde that is attacked by \text{OH}^- (p-nitrobenzaldehyde) is oxidized to the corresponding carboxylate salt (sodium p-nitrobenzoate), while the other aldehyde (p-methoxybenzaldehyde) is reduced to the corresponding alcohol (p-methoxybenzyl alcohol).

In the Grignard reaction, the phenyl group ($\text{Ph}^-$) comes from the Grignard reagent, phenyl magnesium bromide ($\text{PhMgBr}$).

Disconnecting the $\text{C}-\text{Ph}$ bond from the product reveals that the original carbonyl compound must be butan-2-one ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_3$).

Butan-2-one contains a methyl ketone group ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-$), which reacts with $\text{I}_2$ and $\text{NaOH}$ to give a yellow precipitate of iodoform ($\text{CHI}_3$). This confirms the identity of compound 'X' as butan-2-one.
